newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Tapie to have taste of prison.
newsitem.headline: France's Tapie to have taste of prison.

text.p: Fallen soccer boss Bernard Tapie will have to go to prison before France's supreme court rules whether he will stay there for rigging a soccer game, a court said on Monday.

The appeals court in the northern town of Douai rejected a plea from the bankrupt tycoon to avoid having the procedural step of having to surrender ahead of the supreme court (Cour de Cassation) ruling.
The supreme court will rule on February 4 on his appeal against an eight-month prison sentence for rigging a league game between his former club Marseille and Valenciennes in 1993.

Under French law, convicts facing a prison sentence must go to jail before appearing before the supreme court. If the court orders a retrial he will go free but if it rejects his appeal he will go back to jail to serve his term.
Tapie, who has admitted being terrified of going to jail, is also appealing against another prison sentence for tax fraud.
He also goes on trial again on May 12 on suspicion of falsifying Marseille's accounts in order to rig matches and transfers.

Tapie's downfall began shortly after he took Marseille to the European Cup title in 1993. A former cabinet minister, he has since been declared bankrupt and stripped of his seat in the French National Assembly and faces losing his last political job -- his seat in the European Parliament.
